title: P02 oxygen lower bounds pass spatial holdouts, but temporal failures depend on heat and salt limits
abstract: We test whether local source-library gaps can create apparent P02 oxygen loss in 2004-2022. We use measured sources at 0-2000 dbar, conserve Absolute Salinity and Conservative Temperature within stated limits, and compute the lowest oxygen of any nonnegative mixture. At 180-160 W on density 26.6, all same-year cast and whole-bin holdouts have physical support and none falls below its oxygen lower bound. With sources within 10 degrees longitude, the 2004-2022 test has 29 of 34 physically supported targets. Eight remain below the lower bound after adverse independent 1% oxygen scale errors. Whole-bin omission leaves seven failures among 28 supported targets. But widening heat and salt limits from 0.01 g/kg and 0.02 C to 0.02 g/kg and 0.05 C leaves only two stressed failures; 0.05 g/kg and 0.10 C leaves none. These wider limits are stress scenarios, not measured errors. Full-section sources also remove the lower-bound failures. The controls support a temporal mismatch under the tight local null, but the evidence does not determine a ventilation share, local respiration rate or a realizable source transport. The bundle contains code, regional aggregate evidence, figures, exact source hashes and a retrieval recipe. Raw and record-level data stay external.

display.caption: Whole-bin source omission applied to same-year controls and temporal tests. Orange is below the adverse oxygen-error lower bound. Grey has no heat and salt source support. Green means no lower-bound failure, not a full chemical fit.
On density 26.6, local 2004-to-2022 oxygen lower-bound failures decline as the physical mismatch limits widen. The limits are explicit stress scenarios.
